name: global_theorem_independent_audit
statement: The global exponential entropy-rigidity proof (weighted two-shadow compression + entropy-sharpened residual rank, dossier pp.29-36) passed independent review after six precise repairs: (1) expose the disjoint U_s blocks in reverse order and write the conditional expectation explicitly; (2) invoke the finite-group one-point theorem rather than informal 'no wrap' language; (3) condition on extra active coordinates when |U_s| > a_s+1; (4) separate the N=0 case before the weighted sum; (5) state how core-only rows and the empty-core case are assigned; (6) formulate the lower endpoint threshold pointwise or subsequentially.
notes: Audit record. Dossier states the theorem is analytic and does not depend on enumerating the harness's finite systems.

name: finite_field_LO_harness_pass
statement: FINITE_FIELD_LO PASS: exhaustive machine verification of the target-uniform two-point finite-field Littlewood-Offord atom bound psi(u) over coefficient multisets; coefficient_multisets=4370, active-support sizes u=2..8, odd primes p<=13 with p>u.
notes: Exhaustive over the stated finite range only; adversarial check, not part of the analytic proof.

name: batching_harness_pass
statement: BATCHING PASS: machine check of the weighted two-shadow batching / greedy exposure bookkeeping; exhaustive_systems=14592 plus random_systems=5000.
notes: The 14592-system arm is exhaustive over its stated class; the 5000 random systems are sampled numerical evidence only. Adversarial check; theorem is analytic (p.37).

name: exposure_congestion_kappa
statement: For each selected witness batch s of the weighted two-shadow batching, let a_s = number of matching pairs removed by that batch and c_s = -log2 psi(a_s+1). The exposure congestion of a batching B is kappa(B) = max_s a_s/c_s, with kappa = 0 if the two-shadow matching is empty. One may minimize kappa over the matching, the witness choices, and the greedy order, but the bounded-congestion theorem only needs one displayed batching certificate.
notes: Fraction a_s/c_s reconstructed from flattened extraction 'max s as cs' [EXTRACTION-UNCERTAIN, corroborated by kappa<=D/beta below]. Walsh crosspolytope has one huge batch with kappa ~ r/log r, so bounded congestion is a genuine hypothesis.

name: kappa_bounds_from_degree_or_support
statement: Let beta = log2(4/3). (a) If every selected witness meets at most D remaining matching pairs, then kappa <= D/beta. (b) If every private row support has size at most s, then kappa <= (s-1)/beta. (c) A maximum-degree bound on the two-shadow graph implies the same conclusion, because every row support spans a clique in the two-shadow graph. Large support is not automatically fatal: what matters is support relative to the entropy loss it certifies.
notes: (b) reconstructed from flattened 'kappa <= s-1 beta' as (s-1)/beta; confirmed by the absolute coefficient 1+2(s-1)/log2(4/3) on p.39. Uses c_s >= beta from the atom bound (p.31).

name: bounded_congestion_linear_quotient
statement: Rooted block with boundary span B = span W and conditional defect L = L_{Q|W}. If the weighted batching has congestion kappa, then (since sum_s c_s <= L and sum_s a_s <= kappa*L) the endpoints of the selected matching form a private core of size at most 2*kappa*L. Repeating the free/never-free entropy argument outside this private core, the never-free private vector contributes at most L additional directions. Hence a coordinate-selector certificate exists with dim((R+B)/B) <= (2*kappa+1)*L.
notes: Conditional on a displayed batching of congestion kappa. Controls quotient rank modulo the WHOLE boundary; it does NOT give connector absorption (see three_arm_NAE_star_absorption_failure, p.42). 'dim R+B / B' reconstructed as dim((R+B)/B).

name: bounded_support_linear_rigidity_coefficient
statement: If every private witness support has size at most s, then kappa <= (s-1)/log2(4/3), and the bounded-congestion quotient theorem gives the absolute coefficient dim((R+B)/B) <= (1 + 2(s-1)/log2(4/3)) * L_{Q|W}. Thus every bounded-support homogeneous high-corank block satisfies genuine linear quotient rigidity; the theorem also covers unbounded support whenever dense witnesses carry proportionate atom loss.
notes: Quotient rigidity only: the three-arm NAE star (p.42) has private support one yet fails absorption, so this coefficient does not close the rooted theorem.

name: simultaneous_witness_basis_exchange
statement: Let E_1,...,E_k be the selected witness rows in deletion order; choose one pivot coordinate p_s from each witness pair. The pivots are distinct and E_s contains no later pivot p_t (t>s), so the matrix (h_s(p_t))_{s,t=1..k} is triangular with nonzero diagonal. Consequently {h_1,...,h_k} united with {e_i : i not in {p_1,...,p_k}} is a coordinate basis, and k <= ell/log2(4/3). All selected dense witnesses can be inserted simultaneously after O(ell) exchanges. If an old selector used a removed pivot Q_{p_s}, select the witness Y_s and add the discrepancy e_s = Q_{p_s} - Y_s: at most one new direction per exchange. Under bounded congestion the exchanged-basis quotient rank remains linear.
notes: ell = entropy defect ell(A). What fails is the stronger hope that ALL remaining rows are paid solely by the number of selected witnesses - ruled out by the Walsh crosspolytope (p.43).

name: connector_absorption_criterion
statement: Write chosen residual generators uniquely as r_a = b_a + p_a, with b_a in B = span W and p_a in P = span Q. On the coefficient space E of generators define P0: E -> P, P0(e_a) = p_a, and Bbar: E -> B/R_<, Bbar(e_a) = b_a + R_<. Then R intersect B is contained in R_< IFF ker P0 is contained in ker Bbar IFF Bbar = T o P0 for some linear map T. For network-type residual matrices it suffices to test the kernel inclusion on a fundamental-cycle basis: every pure boundary dependency exposed by private cancellation must be an ancestor-paid cycle sum.
notes: Converts 'connector compatibility' into a finite algebraic certificate (the common-lift condition). Dossier uses the letter B for both span W and the map; the map is renamed Bbar here. R_< = ancestor-paid space.

name: rooted_linear_theorem_congestion_plus_lift
statement: Bounded batching congestion together with the common-lift condition (ker P0 contained in ker Bbar, equivalently R intersect span W contained in R_<) is a complete rooted linear theorem for the covered structured classes: dim((R+R_<)/R_<) <= (2*kappa+1)*L_{Q|W} with connector absorption R intersect span W contained in R_<.
notes: 'Covered structured classes' is the dossier's own scope phrase; the general homogeneous block is exactly what remains open (p.53). The two hypotheses are genuinely independent: crosspolytope breaks the first, NAE star the second.

name: three_arm_NAE_star_absorption_failure
statement: Fully closed three-arm NAE star: Y_i = x_i + z_i + q in {+-1}, 1<=i<=3, boundary signs W = (x_i,z_i)_{i=1..3}, one private sign Q = (q). Conditional defect L_{Q|W} = 19/27, and every private support has size one. Nevertheless, when R_< = 0, EVERY boundary-preserving sign basis and selector choice creates a nonzero pure boundary residual: a private linear dependence lies in ker P0 but its boundary part does not lie in ker Bbar. Hence neither bounded private support nor bounded incidence degree implies connector absorption.
notes: Flattened '19 27' read as 19/27 and CONFIRMED here by direct enumeration: fibre has 54 points, H(Q|W) = 8/27, L = 19/27. Consequence: the missing hypothesis must encode coherence of boundary labels around cycles or a common lift from private to boundary residuals; the absorption clause cannot just be appended to the bounded-congestion proof.

name: bounded_support_or_degree_implies_absorption
statement: Route: obtain the rooted theorem by adding to the bounded-congestion quotient bound the claim that bounded private support (even support one) or bounded incidence degree forces connector absorption R intersect span W contained in R_<. FAILS: the three-arm NAE star has all private supports of size one and L_{Q|W} = 19/27, yet with R_< = 0 every basis/selector choice produces a nonzero pure boundary residual.
source: dossier p.42 (packet S9); listed again p.52
notes: Condition of failure: connector incoherence around cycles; local sparsity does not control global connector behavior.

name: walsh_crosspolytope_single_batch
statement: Let r = 2^{2t}, H a Walsh-Hadamard matrix, A_r = {+-H_{*j} : 1<=j<=r} (signed columns). The fibre is fully closed; its full dual is the projectivized {(1/r)Hv : v in {+-1}^r}/{+-1}. A bent sign vector has full Walsh support, so one admissible witness meets every edge of a perfect matching: the weighted batching can be a SINGLE batch with a legal one-row basis exchange. Yet every coordinate-basis selector certificate satisfies dcb(A_r) = r - floor(log2(2r)): a rank-(r-d) image of the cube has at least 2^{r-d} points while selector feasibility permits at most 2r signed basis images, so 2^{r-d} <= 2r; the matching construction attains the bound.
source: dossier p.43 (packet S1, S6); kappa remark p.38
notes: Does NOT refute linear rigidity: ell(A_r) = r - log2(2r), so dcb ~ ell. It refutes that selected-row atom charges alone pay the remainder - unused global defect must also be allocated. Its lone batch has kappa ~ r/log r (p.38). Exponents reconstructed from flattened 'r = 22t', '2r-d' [EXTRACTION: r=2^{2t}, 2^{r-d}; bent vectors need even Walsh dimension, consistent].

name: single_dense_batch_pays_remainder
statement: Route: conclude a small residual (or pay all remaining rows) from a single dense matching batch, i.e. charge the remainder by the number of selected witnesses alone. FAILS: the Walsh crosspolytope admits a one-batch weighted batching and a legal one-row exchange, yet dcb(A_r) = r - floor(log2(2r)), which is r - O(log r), not O(1).
source: dossier p.43, p.40; listed p.52 (packet S1, S6)
notes: Condition of failure: witness count small while unused global defect ell remains large; the unused defect must be spent explicitly.

name: rooted_NAE_cycle_family
statement: For n >= 4: A_n = {(a, b_1,...,b_n) in {+-1}^{n+1} : a + b_i + b_{i+1} in {+-1} for all i, indices cyclic}. On the half a=1 the set {i : b_i = 1} is an independent set of the cycle C_n; the a=-1 half is antipodal. Hence |A_n| = 2*L_n (L_n the n-th Lucas number) and ell(A_n) = n - log2 L_n. The fibre is full closed and its projective full dual is exactly D_n = {A, B_i, C_i : i in Z/nZ} with A = e_0, B_i = e_i, C_i = e_0 + e_i + e_{i+1}. The full-dual real matroid is three-connected.
notes: Header: AUDITED EXACT FAMILY. Genuine high-corank cyclic test case; three-connectivity makes it a probe of strategies relying only on coarse matroid connectivity.

name: binary_quotient_count_lower_bound
statement: Let S_n = {0} union {u_i} union {u_i + u_{i+1}} in F_2^n (indices cyclic; |S_n| = 2n+1, u_i the coordinate vectors). For every w-dimensional subspace W of F_2^n: |S_n/W| >= 2n + 1 - 3w. Proof: choose n-w coordinate images forming a quotient basis; removing the other w cycle vertices destroys at most 2w edges, so at least n-2w distinct weight-two basis sums remain, in addition to zero and the n-w singleton images.
notes: Purely binary counting statement; feeds the geometric-distance lower bound via the mod-2 transfer.

name: real_residual_mod2_transfer
statement: To transfer a real signed residual space R (dim d) to the binary quotient: span only the integral witnesses of its actual signed class equalities and the zero class, obtaining a rational subspace R_0 inside R of dimension d_0 <= d. Its saturated integer lattice is primitive, so reduction modulo 2 preserves dimension d_0 and can only merge classes. Translating the full dual D_n by A identifies it (mod 2) with S_n. Hence a feasible real quotient with at most n+1 classes forces d >= ceil(n/3).
notes: Flattened 'd >= ln 3 m' = ceil(n/3). The rationalization step was explicitly re-checked by the audit (p.46).

name: cycle_geometric_distance_exact
statement: dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3) for the rooted NAE cycle family. Lower bound: binary quotient lemma + mod-2 transfer. Upper bound: choose an independent set U in V(C_n) with |U| = ceil(n/3) and quotient by the independent residuals A + B_u, u in U; the remaining signed classes are represented by the components and cliques of C_n - U, at most 1 + (n-|U|) + (n-2|U|) = 2n+1-3|U| <= n+1 classes.
notes: Audit verified: rationalization step, the zero class, all residue classes of n mod 3, endpoint cases of the real-matroid connectivity proof, and that every displayed dual column is a nonloop and noncoloop (closing singleton separation cases).

name: cycle_optimal_selector_basis
statement: Choose an independent dominating set U in C_n of size d = ceil(n/3) whose cyclic gaps have (edge-)length two or three. Put L_u = A + B_u and R = span{L_u : u in U}; the L_u are independent. Orient the cycle: in a length-two gap u-v-u' take basis forms B_v, C_v; in a length-three gap u-v-w-u' take B_v, C_v, C_w. Together with A these are exactly n+1 full-dual forms, linearly independent by backward substitution through each gap. Modulo R: B_u = -A, C_u = B_v, B_w = C_w in the relevant gap cases, so every full-dual form has a signed basis representative with residual in R. Hence dcb(A_n) = dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3).
notes: Explicit optimal certificate, not just an existence bound. Form count checks: sum of gap lengths = n edges, so d gaps contribute n forms, plus A = n+1.

name: cycle_activation_cell_inequality
statement: For u in U let Z_u record whether the residual L_u = A + B_u is active. For every activation pattern z in {0,1}^U, the optimal selector certificate satisfies |(A_n)_z| <= 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, d = ceil(n/3). Proof: on the a=1 half, z records the intersection of an independent set of C_n with U; a length-two gap has 2,1,1 completions and a length-three gap 3,2,1, according to the sum s+t of its endpoint states, both bounded by 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2} (g = gap edge-length). Multiplying over gaps gives 2^{n-d-|z|} completions; antipodality supplies the factor two. Summing the cells: |A_n|/2^{n+1} <= (3/4)^d, i.e. d <= ell(A_n)/log2(4/3).
notes: Solves the cycle in the stronger CELLWISE form needed for recursive entropy charging, not merely a class-count quotient. Exponents 2^{n+1-d-|z|}, 2^{g-1-(s+t)/2}, (3/4)^d reconstructed from flattened extraction; arithmetic re-verified (sum of (g-1) over gaps = n-d, sum of endpoint states = 2|z|).

name: cycle_connector_transversality
statement: Treat the root sign A as the incoming boundary and the B_i as private coordinates. The optimal residuals L_u = A + B_u project to the DISTINCT private coordinates B_u, hence are independent modulo the boundary, and no nontrivial combination becomes a pure boundary form: R intersect span{A} = 0. The optimal cycle certificate is therefore connector-transverse with zero boundary surcharge and satisfies the common-lift criterion automatically.
notes: Strategic reading (dossier's words): rooted NAE cycles are dense enough to refute the constant-one ceiling lemma yet coherent enough to admit the exact rooted certificate; high corank and three-connectivity are not the obstruction - connector incoherence is.

name: rooted_NAE_path_exact
statement: Cutting the cycle gives a rooted NAE path on N vertices with dcb = dgeo = ceil((N-1)/3).
notes: Flattened 'lN-1 3 m' = ceil((N-1)/3). Header: AUDITED EXACT FAMILY.

name: interval_boundary_basis_Cint
statement: Interval with the root and the two endpoints as boundary and the m = N-2 interior vertices private: there is a boundary-preserving basis with d_m = ceil((m+1)/3) and R_m intersect span W = 0. For every m >= 2: d_m <= C_int * L_{Q|W} with C_int = 2/(3 - log2 5) = 2.949539... The stronger activation coefficient 1/log2(4/3) = 2.40942... holds for m = 2 and all m >= 4.
notes: C_int value re-verified numerically (2/(3-log2 5) = 2.9495396...). m = 3 is exceptional (five-point cellwise anomaly) and m = 1 admits no defect-only bound - see small_affine_boundary_exceptions.

name: small_affine_boundary_exceptions
statement: (a) The three-vertex neutral interval (m = 3) has a five-point cellwise anomaly, so only the weaker constant C_int = 2/(3-log2 5) holds there, not the activation coefficient 1/log2(4/3). (b) For ONE private vertex (m = 1), no defect-only bound is possible: L_{Q|W} can tend to zero while one new direction remains; its cost becomes zero only once the two boundary residuals have already been paid by ancestors.
notes: These exceptions dictate how tiny blocks must be assigned in a recursive decomposition: they are genuine obstructions to any pure defect-proportional charging of small blocks.

name: three_connectivity_ceiling_false
statement: The proposed ceiling bound dcb(A) <= ceil(ell(A)) for three-connected blocks is FALSE. The full-dual real matroid of A_n is genuinely three-connected, yet at n = 13: dcb(A_13) = 5 > ceil(13 - log2 521) = 4 (L_13 = 521). Every n = 0 (mod 6) with n >= 42 belongs to an infinite counterexample family.
notes: Arithmetic re-verified: L_13 = 521, ceil(13 - log2 521) = 4 < 5 = ceil(13/3). Header: DISPROVED STRATEGY - REPLACEMENT THEOREM PASSES. The replacement (exact selector distance + activation cells + zero connector intersection for the same family) is stronger in the direction the proof needs.

name: cycle_rigidity_ratio_limit
statement: dcb(A_n)/ell(A_n) -> 1/(3(1 - log2 phi)) = 1.090186... as n -> infinity (phi the golden ratio). So the rooted NAE cycles exceed the constant-one ceiling only by a bounded factor: connectivity alone cannot be a free certificate, but structured cyclic entropy still pays the correct linear cost, and an absolute linear theorem is not threatened.
notes: Value re-verified numerically from dcb ~ n/3 and ell(A_n) = n - log2 L_n ~ n(1 - log2 phi); flattened '1 3(1 - log2 phi)' reconstructed as 1/(3(1-log2 phi)) [confirmed to 6 decimals].

name: constant_one_ceiling_from_three_connectivity
statement: Route: constant-one rigidity, dcb(A) <= ceil(ell(A)), certified by three-connectivity of the full-dual matroid alone. FAILS: rooted NAE cycles are three-connected with dcb(A_13) = 5 > 4 = ceil(ell(A_13)), and every n = 0 (mod 6), n >= 42 gives an infinite family.
source: dossier p.51; listed p.52 (packet S1, S10, S11)
notes: Condition of failure: coarse matroid connectivity carries no entropy information; the asymptotic ratio is 1.090186... > 1.

name: fixed_q_evaluation_rado
statement: Route: fixed-q evaluation-Rado lower bounds (qev(A) >= r - C*ell(A) with a fixed evaluation prime/point) valid for ALL three-connected blocks. FAILS: the same genuine three-connected rooted NAE cycle family that kills the ceiling bound also defeats the fixed-q evaluation-Rado proposal.
source: dossier p.51; listed p.52 (packet S1, S10, S11)
notes: The intrinsic evaluation-Rado formulation of the target (p.28, outside this digest's range) is not disproved as a TARGET; what fails is deriving it from three-connectivity with fixed q.

Each ruled-out claim has a concrete witness among rooted NAE cycles, the Walsh crosspolytope, and the three-arm NAE star.

name: first_uncovered_homogeneous_block
statement: After all audited reductions, the first uncovered homogeneous block is a singleton-layer cyclic strongly connected component of relation corank at least five. It is not in any solved class (rooted-NAE, stable-set, median, paired-Gale, bounded-congestion). In every useful junction basis it either has congestion at least of order log n in the endpoint range, or fails the common-lift condition.
notes: This is the precise boundary of the covered territory as of the dossier: both known hypotheses fail simultaneously on this block type.

name: rooted_linear_rigidity_target
statement: Target deterministic theorem (open): for every rooted homogeneous block, dim((R + R_<)/R_<) <= C * L_{Q|W} together with connector absorption R intersect span W contained in R_<, for an absolute constant C. Known constraint: any universal C must be at least 1/log2(4/3) = 2.40942... (product of NAE three-circuits, p.28).
source: dossier p.53 (packet S1, S6, S9); target restated from p.28
notes: Flattened 'dim R + R< / R<' = dim((R+R_<)/R_<). This is the rooted statement the block-tree recursion needs; proved so far only under bounded congestion + common lift (p.41) and for the exact families (pp.44-50).

Every connector dependency exposed by this iteration must be assigned to an ancestor-paid fundamental cycle or split off as a lower block.
notes: A concrete plan, not a result. It is exactly the ledger's guidance operationalized: spend unused defect, track cycle sums.

name: sharp_rademacher_singularity_conjecture
statement: Sharp Rademacher singularity conjecture: for B_n an n x n matrix with iid uniform {-1,+1} entries, Pr(det B_n = 0) = (1+o(1)) * 2 * n^2 * 2^{-n} as n -> infinity. The exponential rate (2^{-n+o(n)} scale) is known (Tikhomirov 2018/2020); the sharp polynomial-prefactor version is OPEN. The dossier's final status names it unproved.
source: dossier p.54 (final status); formula per campaign brief / dossier front matter
notes: The formula is not restated verbatim on pp.37-54; p.54 refers to 'the sharp iid Rademacher singularity conjecture'. Flattened '2n22-n' elsewhere in the dossier = 2*n^2*2^{-n}.
